newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Croesus halts gold plant over native title.
newsitem.headline: Croesus halts gold plant over native title.

text.p: Croesus Mining NL said on Friday that it had postponed construction of a A$21 million gold treatment plant at its Binduli gold mine in Western Australia due to unresolved native title negotiations.
The postponement was due to unresolved matters with a native title claimant negotiating with the company, Croesus said.

"The board considers it imprudent at the present time to proceed with construction of the plant until the leases subject to the native title process are clear of the lengthy process," Croesus executive chairman Ron Manners said in a statement.
Manner said Croesus hoped to resume negotiations with the claimant shortly.
"Our oxide reserves combined with a potential opportunity for our existing Haman South Mill will allow us to continue our operation at current levels," Manners said.
Croesus previously had earmarked A$7.1 million in exploration funding for Binduli. The funds are now to be partially diverted to other projects, Manners said.
Under federal native title legislation, aborigines can lay claim to properties they otherwise hold no legal title to and take the action before the courts.
"This is a difficult concept to explain to international investors at a time when many other countries competing for exploration dollars are improving the certainty of mining title," Manners said.
Croesus owns 100 percent of the Binduli project.
